jobs.description:
OBJECTIVES OF THE PROGRAMME

The European Region (EURO) of WHO is made of 53 countries, with over 880 million people. The diversity of people and health situations requires a solid understanding of the emerging socio-economic, epidemiologic, and demographic patterns and trends at regional, national and sub-national levels, with due sensitivity to disadvantaged populations and vulnerable segments of the society. It is equally crucial to have a solid understanding of the commonalities and divergences of the health systems, the circumstances and political economy under which they have evolved and operate. The Division of Programme Management ensures the technical excellence of WHO/Europe's work. It coordinates and ensures coherence across WHO/Europe's health programmes, country support and the Special Initiative on Primary Health Care (PHC).The division also leads planning and budgeting, resource mobilization and partnerships, communications and publications, governance and external relations and language services.

**Description Of Duties

**Under the direct supervision of the Director Programme Management and in close collaboration with the Director Business Operations and the Technical Directors, the incumbent:

• 
Leads the Regional Office's work in the areas of external relations, communications and publications, language services, and governing bodies.

• 
Provides high level strategic support through provision of policy, managerial and diplomatic advice to senior management.

• 
Promotes a culture of high performance, team work, ethical behaviour and integrity in accordance with the Organization's policies, rules and procedures.

• 
Provides support to the DPM in monitoring the implementation of the Global Policy Group of WHO (GPG) decisions and the strategic directions of WHO's work in the Region;

• 
Builds partnerships and contributes to effective and efficient three level coordination in the areas of responsibility, ensuring that countries benefit from the best possible support and advice from WHO headquarters, Regional Office and country office resources.

• 
Oversees and ensures rapid and clear information flows with other regions and WHO headquarters in areas of responsibility.

• 
Contributes to WHO regional coordination and serves as a member of EURO's Executive Council.

• 
Coordinates the work of the technical secretariat for WHO governing body meetings (World Health Assembly, WHO Executive Board, Regional Committee and the Standing Committee of the Regional Committee) and other senior management and advisory meetings.

• 
Interacts with technical directors to ensure implementation of policy decisions of WHO governing bodies

• 
Performs any other duties assigned by the 1st and/or 2nd level supervisor.

**Required Qualifications

**Education

Essential: Advanced university degree in public health, international relations, communications, social sciences or business management.

Desirable: Training in public health related issues.

**Experience

**Essential: At least 15 years of national and international experience with some years at the international level in a senior management position including experience in developing countries. Extensive writing and communications experience. Experience in multipartner health programme management and leadership. Experience guiding and interpreting WHO rules and procedures, including close familiarity with the work of the Regional Office and WHO governing bodies.

Desirable: Experience in the political and/or diplomatic arena.

**Skills

**

• 
Ability to exercise leadership and to work effectively with colleagues at national and international levels;

• 
Diplomatic skills;

• 
Ability to negotiate and engage in new partnerships;

• 
Ability to coordinate teams with different backgrounds in a multicultural environment;

• 
Excellent writing skills in English in a variety of styles and under tight deadline pressure;

• 
Ability to develop messaging and positioning for an international organization;

• 
Demonstrated networking skills, excellent interpersonal skills;

• 
Thorough understanding of public health and international development issues, with the ability to quickly understand, process and communicate new information;

• 
Proven ability to plan, execute, collaborate and work independently with donors, partners, etc.

**WHO Competencies

**

• 
Teamwork*

• 
Respecting and promoting individual and cultural differences*

• 
Communication*

• 
Producing results

• 
Moving forward in a changing environment

• 
Creating an empowering and motivating environment*

Use of Language Skills

Essential: Expert knowledge of English.

Desirable: Intermediate knowledge of French, German and/or Russian.

REMUNERATION

WHO salaries for staff in the Professional category are calculated in US dollars. The remuneration for the above position comprises an annual base salary starting at USD 117,953 (subject to mandatory deductions for pension contributions and health insurance, as applicable), a variable post adjustment, which reflects the cost of living in a particular duty station, and currently amounts to USD 6871 per month for the duty station indicated above. Other benefits include 30 days of annual leave, allowances for dependent family members, home leave, and an education grant for dependent children.

**Additional Information

**

• 
Staff members separated due to the 2025 Prioritization and Realignment Process will receive special consideration according to the applicable regulatory framework.

• 
This vacancy notice may be used to fill other similar positions at the same grade level.

• 
Only candidates under serious consideration will be contacted.

• 
A written test and/or an asynchronous video assessment may be used as a form of screening.

• 
In the event that your candidature is retained for an interview, you will be required to provide, in advance, a scanned copy of the degree(s)/diploma(s)/certificate(s) required for this position. WHO only considers higher educational qualifications obtained from an institution accredited/recognized in the World Higher Education Database (WHED), a list updated by the International Association of Universities (IAU)/United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). The list can be accessed through the link: http://www.whed.net/. Some professional certificates may not appear in the WHED and will require individual review.

Due regard will be paid to the importance of recruiting the staff on as wide a geographical basis as possible.

Any appointment/extension of appointment is subject to WHO Staff Regulations, Staff Rules and eManual.

The Director-General retains the discretion to not make any appointment to this vacancy, to make an appointment at a lower grade, or to make an appointment with a modified job description, including shortening the duration of the appointment.

Agentic AI & Java, SitaWare Insight

• Establishing and maintaining technology standards, and evaluating new technologies as they emerge

**Joining the team

**You will join a growing team within the SitaWare Insight program, close to 50 engineers, architects and testers across five Scrum teams, spanning Aarhus and Copenhagen. We are building a brand-new team around this role:

an architect, a data scientist, five to seven developers and a tester, working closely with our Product Manager and UX designer. You should expect around two to four weeks of travel per year, giving you the chance to collaborate across our Aarhus and Copenhagen teams.

jobs.occupation: Declaration of interest regarding PhD project: The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy
jobs.description:
Declaration of interest regarding PhD project:

The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy, with background in one or more of the following areas: philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, phenomenology.
We are looking for a person with a relevant degree (M.A., MSc. etc.) in philosophy or a related field. Starting date is September 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is fully funded, full-time, for three years. The PhD degree will be awarded by the Faculty of Health Sciences.

 

Research environment

The PhD student will be based in the research group of Applied and Interdisciplinary Phenomenology in the Department of Psychology, SDU, at the Odense campus. The research group develops, disseminates, and applies methods to support cutting-edge research into subjectivity and the nature of human experience. Current group members have backgrounds in philosophy, psychology, anthropology, neuroscience, environmental studies, and pain research.

The group directly supports the professional development of its members, most of whom are postdocs or PhD students. In addition to receiving support from the project team, the PhD student will be supported by the broader group to develop their research, presentation, and teaching skills, as well as other academic skills, including those required for organizing academic activities such as workshops and conferences and for successful grant-writing. The PhD student will therefore be provided with the requisite knowledge and skills for pursuing an academic career in Europe or abroad.

The PhD student will also be provided with a work computer and a dedicated workspace at the Department of Psychology.

 

Project description

The PhD student will be part of the project, Understanding Experiences of Mood Disturbances in Depression (DEPMOOD), led by Anthony Vincent Fernandez. The project is funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark and runs for four years, starting September 1st, 2026. The PhD student will join the project for the final three years, collaborating with the PI, a psychology postdoc, and several external partners in Europe and the US, including philosophers, clinical psychologists, and psychiatrists.

The aim of the project is to establish a taxonomy of the variety of mood disturbances experienced by people diagnosed with depression, providing more precise characterizations of symptoms than those currently offered by concepts such as “depressed mood” or “anhedonia”. The project combines philosophical and qualitative methods, and includes in-depth interviews with people diagnosed with depression. The PhD student will not be expected to carry out interviews, as these will be conducted by the postdoc and external project partners. The PhD student’s primary role will be to help analyze the interview data using a combination of qualitative and philosophical methods. Their PhD thesis will therefore be a theoretical contribution, but will build upon the project’s empirical dataset.

In addition to producing a thesis, the PhD student will be required to take a variety of short PhD courses, carry out an international research stay, and fulfil light teaching duties.

The PhD student will be provided with DKK 10,000 per year for travel. Additional funds may be available.

 

Qualifications

Before the start date of September 1st, 2027, the applicant should have a master’s degree in philosophy or a related field and total course credits equivalent to 300 ECTS. Typically, this is a total of at least five years of education combined between bachelor’s and master’s degrees, with 60 ECTS obtained for every full year of study.

The candidate should have a background in philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, and/or phenomenology. Familiarity with qualitative research methods (especially analysis methods) is an advantage, but by no means required.

The candidate should be proficient in English. Proficiency in Danish or another Scandinavian language may be an advantage, but is not required.

For further information about the project, please contact:
Anthony Vincent Fernandez

Department of Psychology

University of Southern Denmark (SDU)

E-mail: afernandez@health.sdu.dk

Please note that while we are happy to provide answers to questions about the position and application process, direct feedback on application materials cannot be provided.

Applications must include (in English, or with a certified English translation):

 

• 
A letter stating the interest, motivation and qualifications for the project (max. 2 pages) - upload under “Application form”.

• 
Detailed CV, including personal contact information as well as any publications or presentations

• 
Certified copy of diploma and transcripts (Master’s degree in a relevant field). If the applicant is in the process of completing their master’s degree, they should provide transcripts along with a letter from their supervisor confirming expected completion of their degree before September 1st, 2027.

• 
Writing sample of maximum 10,000 words (e.g., publication, conference paper, selection from a master’s thesis). If the sample exceeds this length, please indicate which section should be read.

• 
A document listing 2-3 references, with contact information and a brief note about your relation to the reference. Note that reference letters will only be requested for candidates invited to interview.

 

At this stage, no project proposal is required. Candidates invited to interview will be asked to prepare a brief project plan.

Please do not use generative AI in the formulation of any application materials. The purpose of these materials is to gain a clear sense of you and your abilities.

Shortlisting and interviews may be used in the assessment process.
 

For purposes of evaluation and assessment, application materials may be shared with external members of the project team at Aarhus University and Amsterdam University Medical Center.

Further information about the PhD-study can be found at the homepage of the University.

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now". Attached files must be in Adobe PDF format. We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.

Incomplete applications and applications received after the deadline will neither be considered nor evaluated

 

Closing date January 15th, 2027

 

We expect to conduct interviews within two months of the application closing date.
Successful candidates will be asked to send an application to the PhD Secretariat, Faculty of Health Sciences, to be enrolled as PhD students.
 

The PhD programme will be carried out in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order)

 

Salary and Working Conditions at SDU

PhD students employed at SDU are employed as PhD fellows according to the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations in public employment (AC) agreement.

Salary and any salary supplement are paid according to your seniority level and as negotiated with your union representative. The base salary (excluding 18.07% pension contribution) is DKK 374,912.98   per year.

The Faculty of Health Sciences at the University of Southern Denmark is one of Denmark’s leading faculties of health sciences. With nine departments, internationally top‑class research, and a broad range of health‑related study programmes, we contribute to developing the knowledge, treatments, and healthcare system of the future.

As an employee at the faculty, you become part of an ambitious and interdisciplinary environment characterised by high academic standards, strong collaborations, and excellent opportunities for professional development. The faculty has activities in Odense, Esbjerg, and Copenhagen. In Esbjerg and Copenhagen, strong academic communities provide the framework for research and education, while our modern faculty building in Odense brings research, education, and administration together under one roof and is directly connected to Odense University Hospital.

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: Four-year Researcher position on Greenland marine ecosystems
jobs.description:
Four-year Researcher position on Greenland marine ecosystems
The Department of Ecoscience, Aarhus University, invites applications for a four-year scientist position on the biodiversity and coastal ecosystem status and trends along Greenland’s coast with a special focus on the use of eDNA for monitoring of marine macroalgae. The position is linked to multiple international projects, including the Greenland Ecosystem Monitoring Programme with an overarching theme of studying the impacts of climate change on coastal ecosystems in Greenland. The position requires active participation in developing and attracting funding for new projects including a special focus on developing and implementing eDNA tools for the ecological research and monitoring.

This is a four–year position available from 15 February 2027. 

Job description
The position focuses on the ecology of coastal marine ecosystems in Greenland and their responses to climate change, particularly warming and the ongoing loss of the cryosphere.

You are expected to participate in annual field campaigns in Greenland and contribute to the analysis and interpretation of monitoring and experimental data from coastal Greenland ecosystems. A particular focus will be on developing and applying environmental DNA (eDNA) methods for characterising and quantifying marine biodiversity, with an emphasis on marine macroalgae. This includes establishing high-quality biodiversity baselines and improving our capacity to detect changes in species distributions and the arrival of new species.

Your profile
Applicants must hold a PhD in biology or a closely related field. Documented experience with Arctic marine vegetation and ecosystem ecology is considered an advantage, together with expertise in eDNA-based approaches, including metabarcoding, quantitative PCR-based methods such as digital PCR (dPCR), bioinformatics and biostatistics.

Experience with marine fieldwork, DNA barcoding, experimental design and morphological species identification is also an advantage. The successful candidate is expected to have experience in developing research ideas and in contributing to research proposals and grant applications. A scientific diving certification is considered an advantage.

Fluency in spoken and written English is required. In addition, the candidate should enjoy working collaboratively in an interdisciplinary and international research environment and be motivated to contribute actively to fieldwork, research development and scientific publication.

Who we are
The Department of Ecoscience (https://ecos.au.dk/en/) is organised under the Faculty of Technical Sciences. The department’s research areas cover most aspects of biology and ecology, spanning all biological levels from genetics, physiological processes, individuals, populations and species to entire ecosystems. Strategic and applied research account for a large part of the research activities at the Department of Ecoscience. Geographically, the department works from the tropics to the poles, but with greater focus on Danish conditions. The department has an obligation towards the Ministry of Environment and Food of Denmark and the authorities in Greenland as national advisors on environmental issues. The department’s research, consultancy and teaching are linked to strong and active research groups. 

What we offer 
The successful candidate is offered:

• Access to a well-developed research infrastructure
• Office space and shared equipment
• a research climate inviting lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
• a working environment with teamwork, close working relations, network activities among young scientists and social activities
• a workplace characterized by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance
Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work is the main University campus in Aarhus, C.F. Møllers Allé 3, 8000 Aarhus C. 

Contact information

For further information, please contact Mikael Sejr (mse@ecos.au.dk) or Dorte Krause-Jensen (dkj@ecos.au.dk). 

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. 

Formalities and salary range 
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

The Danish Resilience Agency (SAMSIK) is seeking a highly experienced and strategic leader to serve as Head of the Nordic-Baltic Cyber Consortium (NBCC).

• 
Provide overall strategic direction and leadership of the NBCC in line with EU objectives, consortium agreements and national mandates.

• 
Develop, implement and continuously adjust the NBCC’s strategic roadmap, including the phased build-up from initial deployment to full operational capability.

• 
Ensure alignment between the NBCC activities, EU cybersecurity policies and the strategic interests of participating member states.

Are you motivated by turning complex customer requirements into competitive and commercially robust proposals? Do you thrive on creating structure, coordinating specialists, and driving tender processes from opportunity to contract award? Then you could be our new Tender Manager.

Your position 

As our new Tender Manager, you will play a key role in securing renewable offshore service opportunities, with a particular focus on offshore wind. You will lead the complete tender lifecycle, from initial qualification and bid strategy through proposal development, internal approval, submission, clarification, negotiation, and handover to project delivery. 

Working closely with colleagues across Sales, Engineering, Operations, Legal, Finance, Procurement, and HSEQ, you will bring together the right expertise and turn complex requirements into clear, compliant, and customer-focused solutions. You will create structure throughout the process, maintain tender governance, manage commercial risks, and ensure that every submission is delivered on time and to a high standard. 

In this full-time position you will report to the Sales Director, Service. Your place of work will be Esbjerg, Aarhus, Copenhagen or Grimsby, UK and travelling for customer meetings, site visits, negotiations, and other tender-related activities should be expected. 

At Semco Maritime, safety is a core value. In this role, you will contribute to maintaining a strong culture of safety, quality, compliance, and integrity throughout all tender activities.

Your tasks & responsibilities 
As Tender Manager, you will be responsible for planning, coordinating, and delivering assigned tenders while ensuring clear ownership, effective collaboration, disciplined governance, and alignment with our commercial objectives. 

Your tasks will include, but are not limited to:

• Leading renewable offshore service tenders from qualification and bid/no-bid assessment through submission, negotiation, award, and structured handover.
• Establishing tender strategies, plans, timelines, responsibilities, review gates, and communication routines across the bid team.
• Coordinating technical, operational, commercial, contractual, procurement, finance, and HSEQ contributions into coherent and compelling proposals.
• Managing pricing inputs, assumptions, exclusions, compliance, risks, opportunities, clarifications, and internal approval processes.
• Preparing and quality-assuring customer-focused submissions while capturing lessons learned and contributing to the continuous improvement of tender processes, tools, and content.
Your profile & qualifications 

We are looking for a commercially aware and structured tender professional who enjoys bringing people and specialist disciplines together around a shared deadline. You take ownership, maintain an overview when the process becomes complex, and communicate clearly with stakeholders at different levels of the organisation. 

You combine attention to detail with the ability to understand the bigger commercial picture. You are comfortable challenging inputs, following up on deliverables, and ensuring that the proposed solution is both competitive and operationally achievable. 

To succeed in this position, we imagine that you have: 

• Relevant experience in tender or bid management within offshore wind, renewable energy, maritime, oil and gas, engineering, or technical services. 
• Experience leading complex, multidisciplinary tenders involving several internal and external stakeholders. 
• A strong understanding of tender governance, compliance, cost estimation, pricing, contractual risk, approvals, negotiations, and handovers. 
• Excellent written English and strong communication, editing, planning, and stakeholder-management skills. 
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office and relevant tender, CRM, document-management, or collaboration platforms. 

Additional languages relevant to our key markets will be considered an advantage. 

Welcome to Semco Maritime

At Semco Maritime, we create change. For people. For projects. And for the global energy sector. With us, you will join a community of over 2,300 of the most dedicated thinkers and doers in the energy industry who are driving real change and making their own personal mark on the global energy landscape.

While everyone knows why the energy transition is vital, we are concerned with the journey. How to get there. By providing the answers needed to make change real. Because we believe that global energy ambitions can only be realized through hard work and clever pragmatic solutions. This is what we do. This is what we invite you to participate in.

Safety is at the core of everything we do, and we are committed to protecting our people, partners, and the planet as we work towards a sustainable energy future.

So yes, working for us will change the energy sector – and may well change you too. 

We know that our people are our greatest strength. We strive to build an inclusive workplace where everyone can be themselves, contribute their perspectives, and feel part of the team. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and believe that diverse teams help us find better solutions and move the energy transition forward.  

Care to join the movement?
Change. With us.

Semco Maritime is an international engineering and contracting company with 2,300 employees and 40 years of dedication rooted in both the conventional energy sector and the offshore wind industry. This puts us in a unique position to bridge today's and tomorrow’s solutions, constantly seeking clever and pragmatic ways to realise global energy ambitions. We do this through comprehensive project management across all phases of energy projects together with world-leading partners across the globe.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in fungal genomics and predictive modelling - DTU Food
jobs.description:
Fungi are increasingly causing health issues globally. Such infections are not only increasing in humans and animals, but also in crops and as contamination of food products with mycotoxins.

We have recently been awarded funding to develop online webservices for genomic characterization of all pathogens capable of infecting animals, humans and plants, which includes fungi. However, genomics methods and workflows have so far not gained enough attention in relation to plant infecting or mycotoxin producing fungi. 

Databases of genomes of known fungal species have already been developed, as has gene databases of mycotoxin producing gene clusters, but an extensive linkage to fungal taxa is poorly described. Furthermore, it is known that a number of fungi including some used in food production have the gene cluster for mycotoxin production but do not express them.

There is an urgent need to improve our understanding of the genomics of fungi, as well as to translate this into online services.

Thus, as part of our GPAP project (www.gpap.global) and our responsibilities as advise provider to the Danish Food Administration we are seeking a PhD-candidate in fungal genomics with a focus on correlating genomes to phenotypes and developing webservices. This will include whole genome sequencing of fungi, culturing and phenotypic characterization and implementing tools in our widely used online webservice.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your main responsibility will be to create a webservice for identifying fungal taxa, mycotoxin-producing gene clusters and predict phenotypes under different growth conditions. You will perform complete genome sequencing (including the analyses) of a selected range of fungal to create an improved database of reference genomes.

You will also:

• develop a web-based tool for species identification and detection of known toxin-gene clusters, virulence genes and regulatory genes.
• conduct phenotype to genotype association studies based on a large collection of phenotypically characterized Fusarium isolates and develop and improve the online tool.
• With assistant from other group members, you will analyse the output, draw conclusions and present the outputs. 
• communicate research results by presenting data at project meetings and international conferences and write reports and manuscripts for publication.
• engage in the general work carried out by the research group, including discussions and planning of strategies and projects, drafting research grant proposals, etc.
Daily work will be in close collaboration with other researchers in the Genomic Epidemiology group at DTU Food and the Applied Mycology group at DTU Bioengineering, as well as national and international partners.

The ideal candidate has experience in coding in python and experience with Unix-based systems and in machine and deep learning.

Other desired qualifications are:

• extensive knowledge in microbial genomics including phylogenetic analysis
• extensive knowledge of existing bioinformatic algorithms and tools.
• experience with DNA-based workload from microbes
It is a great advantage if you have experience in general microbiology and preferably fungal culturing.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The period of employment is 3 years. Starting date is 1 February 2027 (or according to mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
The position is a collaboration between DTU Food and DTU Bioengineering, with the employment at DTU-Food. Further information may be obtained from Associate professor Christian Brinch, cbri@food.dtu.dk or Associate professor Jakob Blæsbjerg Hoof, jblni@dtu.dk.

You can read more about DTU National Food Institute at DTU National Food Institute and DTU Bioengineering at DTU Bioengineering .

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 10 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU National Food Institute
DTU National Food Institute conducts research into and disseminates - through advice, innovation and teaching - sustainable and value-creating solutions in the area of food and health for the benefit of society. The vision is to make a difference by generating future prosperity through research into food and health. The institute works to prevent disease and promote health, develop new and better food products for a growing population and create sustainable technological solutions, including biosolutions. The institute’s tasks are carried out in interdisciplinary collaboration within e.g. nutrition, chemistry, toxicology, microbiology, epidemiology, modelling, and technology. This is achieved through a strong academic environment of international top class with correspondingly skilled researchers and employees. The Institute employs approximately 390 staff members.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: Engineer - Power System Analytics; DK - Fredericia
jobs.description:
Do you want to contribute to the secure and stable operation of the Danish power system as renewable energy continues to grow? You will combine power system engineering, data analytics and applied research to develop methods and tools that support system stability and the management of critical power system events.

Join our power system specialists

At our head office in Fredericia you join a department responsible for supporting the secure and stable operation of the Danish power system, both today and in the future with an increasing share of renewable energy. We develop methods, analyses and digital solutions that support system stability, security of supply and the handling of major disturbances.  As part of Energinet’s System Operations organisation, we work closely with the Control Centre, IT specialists and international transmission system operators.

The department consists of 18 colleagues organised into two groups. Together, we combine knowledge in power system operations, grid analysis, system stability, data analytics, and digital solution development. You become part of an inter-national and collaborative environment where we use both Danish and English in our daily work. 

Develop methods and tools for system stability

You contribute to developing next-generation dynamic stability assessment, system monitoring, and power system restoration capabilities for an electricity system increasingly based on renewable energy. 

Your primary responsibilities include:

• analysing power system dynamics, stability and disturbance events using PowerFactory and PSCAD
• developing and applying methods based on PMU and other operational measurement data
• identifying stability risks and proposing mitigation measures together with operational specialists
• supporting the digitalisation and automation of processes related to Dynamic Stability Assessment
• collaborating with operational specialists, software developers, researchers and external partners across the Nordic and European power sector

“You join a specialised environment where we share knowledge, ask questions and solve complex technical challenges together.”
– Nan Qin, Team Leader

Bring your technical curiosity

You have a relevant background in electrical engineering, power systems or a related technical discipline. You may be newly graduated or have some professional experience. Experience with power system analysis, dynamic simulations, PowerFactory, programming, measurement data or digital tool development is an advantage.

Most importantly, you are curious, structured and keen to learn. You ask questions and seek input when needed, while also taking responsibility for your own analyses. You enjoy teamwork, and you are equally comfortable addressing complex technical questions on your own.

Will you make a difference with us?

We look forward to receiving your motivated CV no later than 8 November. You may want to pencil in a couple of dates in your calendar already. We expect the first interview to take place online on 13 November and the second interview in Fredericia on 19 November.

If you have questions about the job, please contact Thue Søndergård Thomsen, Head of Department, on mail THSTH@energinet.dk.

Special conditions: As Energinet performs tasks critical to society, we carry out background checks prior to employment. Employment is conditional upon your background check being compatible with employment at Energinet. The background check is also carried out once a year.

The position also requires that you are able to obtain and maintain security clearance. On PET's website, you can read more about security clearance.

We see diversity as a strength and encourage all qualified people, regardless of background, to apply for the job. We work actively and determinedly with diversity in Energinet and therefore encourage you to exclude information about age, marital status, etc. to minimise outage biases in the process. You can read more about our diversity policy here.

Energinet Systemsansvar's core tasks are to integrate renewable energy, ensure equal access to the grids, develop market design, monitor, and balance the transmission grid and ensure security of supply in Denmark. We are a subsidiary of the Energinet Group, which represents the interests of society when supplying Denmark with electricity and gas and that the energy system is converted to green energy. Our culture is closely linked to our social responsibility, and we work actively with the UN's global goals on sustainable energy, climate action, partnerships for action as well as industry, innovation, and infrastructure. By leading the way in the green transition, we can help to solve the global climate challenge. New solutions require us to be able to see problems from many different angles, and diversity is therefore a keyword in our culture. We strive to listen to, involve and share our knowledge. Based on the values of courage and trust, we focus on constantly developing ourselves as an organisation and as people. Read more at our website www.energinet.dk.

jobs.occupation: Demand Planner
jobs.description:
Are you structured, analytical, and motivated by ensuring that products are available when our customers need them?

We are looking for a Demand Planner to support the daily planning and replenishment of our warehouse assortment and help ensure the right balance between product availability and inventory.

In this role, you will work hands-on with demand forecasts, replenishment, purchase orders, inventory levels, and planning exceptions. You will be an important link between Sales, Procurement, Warehouse, Operations, and our suppliers and factories, helping turn demand into clear and executable supply requirements.

Your key responsibilities

• 
Maintain and update demand forecasts based on sales history, trends, customer input, and changes in demand.

• 
Plan replenishment and ensure timely ordering of products for our warehouse assortment.

• 
Follow up on open purchase orders, delivery dates, and expected incoming supply.

• 
Monitor stock levels and identify potential shortages, excess inventory, and availability risks.

• 
React to changes in demand and supply and adjust plans accordingly.

• 
Follow up on service level, forecast accuracy, inventory, and other operational planning KPIs.

• 
Work closely with Sales, Procurement, Warehouse, and Operations to resolve day-to-day planning and availability issues.

• 
Maintain high-quality planning parameters and master data.

• 
Support improvements to planning processes, systems, and ways of working.

Who are you?

You have experience within demand planning, replenishment, purchasing, inventory management, or supply chain planning and enjoy working in a role where you are close to the daily operation.

You are comfortable working with numbers, data, and planning systems and have a structured approach to managing priorities and following up on deviations. Experience with ERP systems, forecasting or replenishment tools, and Excel is an advantage.

As a person, you are structured, proactive, persistent, and solution-oriented. You take ownership of your area, follow issues through to resolution, and communicate clearly with colleagues and stakeholders.

What we offer

You will join an international planning organization and take responsibility for an important part of our daily planning operation. Your work will have a direct impact on product availability, inventory levels, and customer service.

You will work closely with colleagues across Sales, Procurement, Logistics, Warehouse, and Operations and have opportunities to develop your competencies within demand and supply chain planning.

The position is based in Tvis, Holstebro.

Recruitment process

Please submit your application and CV via our recruitment system. Interviews will be conducted on an ongoing basis.

About Actona Group

Actona Group is an international furniture company headquartered in Denmark, operating in more than 90 countries. We develop, source, and sell modern furniture solutions to some of the world's leading retailers and private label customers.

We are on a continuous journey towards becoming a larger, stronger, and more sustainable company. We aim to create continued growth and value-adding services for the benefit of our customers and partners while minimizing our environmental impact.

Facts about Actona Group:

• 
2,500 employees worldwide

• 
Headquarters, showroom, and European distribution centre in Tvis, Denmark

• 
Furniture production and local administration in Lithuania, Poland, and Ukraine

• 
Trading company in China

• 
Part of Lars Larsen Group

jobs.occupation: FRISKSNIT søger medarbejdende teamleder til fødevareproduktion i Hedehusene/FRISKSNIT is hiring a Hands-on Team Leader for Food Production in Hedehusene, Denmark / Permanent, hourly-paid position with 37 paid working hours.
jobs.description:
DANSK:

Timelønnet fuldtidsstilling på 37 timer om ugen – med faste arbejdstider søndag–torsdag og fri fredag–lørdag.

Har du øje for kvalitet, kan du holde overblik, og har du lyst til at tage ansvar for et mindre team? Så søger vi dig til vores fødevareproduktion i Hedehusene.

Hos FRISKSNIT søger vi en medarbejdende teamleder, som både deltager i det praktiske produktionsarbejde og koordinerer opgaverne for tre kolleger. Du skal sammen med teamet sikre, at produkterne bliver pakket korrekt, mærket rigtigt og færdige til tiden.

Vi er en fødevareproduktionsvirksomhed med cirka 75 fuldtidsansatte. Vi er medlem af Dansk Industri og omfattet af Industriens Overenskomst.

Dine arbejdsopgaver

Du bliver ansvarlig for den daglige koordinering i dit team og samarbejder tæt med den produktionsansvarlige. Du deltager selv i produktionen og følger op på, at teamet arbejder effektivt og overholder instruktionerne for kvalitet, hygiejne og sikkerhed.

Dine vigtigste opgaver er at:

• 
Koordinere og fordele arbejdet mellem teamets tre øvrige medarbejdere og følge op på dagens opgaver og effektivitet.

• 
Sikre korrekt pakning og mærkning, herunder kontrollere emballage, etiketter og datomærkning.

• 
Deltage i produktions- og pakkearbejdet samt støtte og oplære kolleger i de aftalte arbejdsgange.

• 
Reagere på fejl og forsinkelser og inddrage den produktionsansvarlige, når der er behov for hjælp eller ændrede prioriteringer.

Hvem er du?

Du arbejder omhyggeligt, tager ansvar og bevarer overblikket, når der er travlt. Du kan give tydelige instruktioner og bidrager til et godt samarbejde gennem en respektfuld og hjælpsom tilgang til dine kolleger.

Erfaring fra fødevareproduktion, pakkeri eller lignende er en fordel, men du behøver ikke have en bestemt faguddannelse. Erfaring med koordinering af opgaver eller oplæring af kolleger er også en fordel. Det er ikke et krav, at du tidligere har haft titlen teamleder.

Arbejdssproget er engelsk. Du skal derfor kunne forstå arbejdsinstruktioner og kommunikere tydeligt med kolleger og ledelse på engelsk.

Arbejdstid:

Stillingen er på 37 betalte arbejdstimer om ugen med følgende faste mødetider:

Søndag: kl. 08.00–16.00
Mandag–torsdag: kl. 12.00–20.00
Fredag og lørdag: fri

Mødetiderne omfatter samlet tre timers ubetalte pauser om ugen. Pauserne indgår ikke i de 37 betalte arbejdstimer. Den konkrete placering af pauserne fremgår af arbejdsplanen.

Arbejdstidens placering følger virksomhedens lokalaftale.

Løn og ansættelsesvilkår:

Du bliver timelønnet med grundtimeløn, et fast teamledertillæg og relevante tillæg, herunder tillæg for søndagsarbejde.

Ansættelsen sker efter Industriens Overenskomst og virksomhedens gældende lokalaftaler, med pension, feriepenge og fritvalg.

Fritvalg og søgnehelligdagsbidrag udbetales månedligt sammen med lønnen efter virksomhedens aftale.

Du får oplæring i arbejdsopgaverne, vores produkter og de kvalitetskrav, der gælder i produktionen. Du får en praktisk rolle med ansvar for den daglige koordinering og tæt samarbejde med både dit team og den produktionsansvarlige.

Ansættelsesform: Tidsubegrænset fuldtidsansættelse.
Arbejdssted: FRISKSNIT, Hedelykken 14, 2640 Hedehusene.
Tiltrædelse: Efter aftale.

Sådan søger du

Send dit CV og en kort ansøgning til Job@frisksnit.dk senest fredag den 13. november 2026. Skriv ”Teamleder – FRISKSNIT” i emnefeltet.

Fortæl gerne om din erfaring med produktion, pakning eller koordinering af kolleger, og hvorfor du er interesseret i stillingen. Du er velkommen til at skrive din ansøgning på engelsk.

Spørgsmål til stillingen kan også sendes til Job@frisksnit.dk.

Vi opfordrer alle kvalificerede ansøgere til at søge stillingen.

ENGLISH

Permanent, hourly-paid position with 37 paid working hours per week – fixed working hours Sunday to Thursday, with Fridays and Saturdays off.

Do you have an eye for quality, enjoy organising daily tasks and want to take responsibility for a small team? Join our food production team in Hedehusene.

At FRISKSNIT, we are looking for a hands-on Team Leader who will take part in production while coordinating the work of three colleagues. Together with your team, you will ensure that products are packed correctly, labelled accurately and ready on time.

We are a food production company with approximately 75 full-time employees. We are a member of the Confederation of Danish Industry (DI) and covered by the Danish Industrial Agreement (Industriens Overenskomst).

Your responsibilities

You will coordinate your team’s daily work and work closely with the person responsible for production. You will also take part in production yourself, helping the team work efficiently and follow our quality, hygiene and safety procedures.

Your main tasks will be to:

• 
Coordinate and allocate tasks among the three other team members and follow up on daily work and productivity.

• 
Ensure correct packing and labelling, including checking packaging, labels and date markings.

• 
Take part in production and packing, while supporting colleagues and training them in the agreed procedures.

• 
Respond to errors and delays and involve the person responsible for production when support or changes to priorities are needed.

About you

You work carefully, take responsibility and stay organised when things get busy. You can give clear instructions and contribute to good teamwork by treating your colleagues with respect and offering support.

Experience in food production, packing or a similar role is an advantage, but no specific vocational qualification is required. Experience coordinating tasks or training colleagues is also an advantage. You do not need to have held a Team Leader position before.

The working language is English. You must be able to understand work instructions and communicate clearly with colleagues and management in English.

Working hours

The position offers 37 paid working hours per week, with the following fixed schedule:

Sunday: 08:00–16:00
Monday–Thursday: 12:00–20:00
Friday and Saturday: Days off

The scheduled hours include a total of three hours of unpaid breaks per week. Breaks are not included in the 37 paid working hours. Break times are specified in the work schedule.

Working hours are arranged under the company’s local agreement.

Pay and employment terms

This is an hourly-paid position with a basic hourly wage, a fixed Team Leader allowance and applicable supplements, including a supplement for Sunday work.

Employment is covered by the Danish Industrial Agreement (Industriens Overenskomst) and the company’s applicable local agreements, including pension contributions, holiday pay and flexible benefits.

Flexible benefits payments (fritvalg) and the public-holiday allowance are paid monthly together with wages under the company’s agreement.

You will receive training in your tasks, our products and the quality requirements that apply in production. The role combines practical work with responsibility for daily coordination and close cooperation with your team and the person responsible for production.

Employment type: Permanent, full-time employment with no fixed end date.
Workplace: FRISKSNIT, Hedelykken 14, 2640 Hedehusene, Denmark.
Start date: By agreement.

How to apply

Please send your CV and a short application to Job@frisksnit.dk by Friday, 13 November 2026. Use “Team Leader – FRISKSNIT” as the email subject.

Tell us about your experience in production, packing or coordinating colleagues, and why you are interested in the position. Applications in English are welcome.

Questions about the position can also be sent to Job@frisksnit.dk.

We welcome applications from all qualified candidates.
